name: League of Nations
summary: The International Telecommunication Union, a specialist agency of the League of Nations, is established. The League of Nations (LN or LoN; French: Société des Nations [sɔsjete de nɑsjɔ̃], SdN) was the first worldwide intergovernmental organisation whose principal mission was to maintain world peace. It was founded on 10 January 1920 by the Paris Peace Conference that ended the First World War.

The 8.0 Nepal–Bihar earthquake strikes Nepal and Bihar with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing an estimated 6,000–10,700 people. The disaster caused major human and material losses and prompted renewed attention to emergency response, public safety, and reconstruction. Its aftermath affected communities and public policy beyond the immediate emergency.

name: French political crisis
summary: French political crisis: The French far-right leagues rally in front of the Palais Bourbon, in an attempted coup d'état against the Third Republic. The event affected the balance of power and shaped subsequent military or political decisions, while its consequences extended beyond the immediate confrontation. It became part of the wider struggle that defined the period.

name: Manchukuo
summary: Manchukuo, the Japanese puppet state in Manchuria established in 1932, proclaimed a monarchy under Puyi. Manchukuo, officially called Manchoukuo, was a puppet state of the Empire of Japan in Manchuria that existed from 1932 until its dissolution in 1945. It was ostensibly founded as a republic, its territory consisting of the lands seized in the Japanese invasion of Manchuria; it was later declared to be a constitutional monarchy in 1934, though very little changed in the actual functioning of government.

name: Prime Minister Konstantin Päts stages a self-coup by declaring a state of...
summary: Prime Minister Konstantin Päts stages a self-coup by declaring a state of emergency in Estonia, with the approval of the parliament, beginning the country's Era of Silence. The political change influenced the direction of government policy and the country's response to the major domestic and international pressures of the period. It also affected later alliances, reforms, or public debates.

name: May Constitution of 1934
summary: The May Constitution of 1934 heralds the beginning of the Austrofascist Federal State of Austria. The agreement altered the legal or political framework surrounding the dispute and influenced the decisions taken by the governments and movements involved. Its implementation shaped later negotiations and relations between the parties.

name: Treaty of Taif
summary: Imam Yahya of Yemen and Ibn Saud of Saudi Arabia conclude a peace treaty. name: July Putsch
summary: July Putsch: Austrian Nazis assassinate chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss, during a failed coup attempt. The July Putsch (German: Juliputsch) was a failed coup d'état in Austria against the Fatherland Front government of Engelbert Dollfuss by Austrian Nazis from 25 to 30 July 1934. The Austrian Legion and Austrian Schutzstaffel soldiers with support from Nazi Germany attempted to depose Dollfuss's Austrofascist regime in favor of a pro-Nazi government under Anton Rintelen of the Christian Social Party.

name: Adolf Hitler
summary: Adolf Hitler becomes Führer of Germany, or head of state combined with that of Chancellor, following the death of President Paul von Hindenburg.
